title: Northern Blot analysis of mRNA from mammalian polyribosomes
protocol: Seed 0.8-1.0 X 10^7 293T cells onto each 15-cm culture dish 1-3 days before polysome fractionation.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C until they reach no more than 70-80% confluency.
Add cycloheximide to a final concentration of 50 μg/ml to the growth medium 48 hours post seeding.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min after adding cycloheximide.
Transfer plate to rest directly on ice in a box or bucket.
Aspirate growth medium, and wash cells with 10 ml of ice-cold PBS containing 50 μg/ml of cycloheximide.
Aspirate the solution, and repeat the wash step.
Scrape cells with a cell lifter, and transfer to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge in a refrigerated microcentrifuge at 7000 rpm for 1 min.
Aspirate supernatant.
Add 250 μl of 2X RSB/RNasin to resuspend cell pellet.
Add 250 μl of polyribosome extraction, and mix quickly.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Spin for 10 sec to pellet nuclei.
Transfer 500 μl of cytoplasmic extract to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 10,000 X g for 10 min at 4°C.

While the cytoplasmic extract is centrifuging, prepare gradients in an ultracentrifuge tube by underlaying 5.5 ml of 10% sucrose solution with 5.5 ml of 50% sucrose solution without disturbing the interface.

Gently insert the tip of a blunt end stainless steel needle to the bottom of the tube and slowly release the 50% sucrose solution from the syringe to displace the 10% sucrose solution upwards in the tube.
Close the tube with a BioComp cap.
Put the capped tubes in the BioComp gradient master.
Select the gradient parameter according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and start the run.
When the gradient formation is finished, carefully remove the cap.
Transfer the tube to an SW41Ti rotor bucket.
Carefully layer on top of gradient an additional 500 μl of 10% sucrose.
During cap insertion, make sure there are no air bubbles trapped inside the tube.
Keep rotor buckets cold throughout the procedure.
When the spin is finished, carefully layer 500 μl of the cytoplasmic extract on top of the sucrose gradient.
(Optional) Add 30 μl of 250 mM EDTA to 470 μl of cleared cytoplasmic extract and layer the extract on a second gradient.
Place rotor buckets in the SW41Ti rotor and centrifuge at 36,000 rpm for 2 h at 4°C.
After centrifugation, remove rotor buckets and keep them in ice until fractions from each tube are collected.

Collect approximately 20 550 μl fractions on ice into 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tubes using the BioComp piston gradient fractionator equipped with a UV-M II monitor connected to the DATAQ DI-154RS data acquisition module.
Add 60 μl of 10% SDS and 12 μl of Proteinase K (10 mg/ml) to each fraction.
Mix and incubate for 30 min at 42°C.
Transfer 300 μl of each Proteinase K-treated fraction to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Extract each fraction twice with 300 μl of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol, keeping tubes on ice between steps.
Extract each fraction once with 300 μl of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol, keeping tubes on ice between steps.
Transfer each supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 30 μl of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 825 μl of 100% ethanol to precipitate RNA from each fraction.
Mix the solution and store at -80°C for 15 min.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 20 min at 4°C to collect RNA pellets.
Wash the RNA pellets with 1 ml of 75% ethanol.
Aspirate supernatant from each tube, leaving the cap open to allow the RNA pellet to dry.
Do not overdry the RNA pellet.
Resuspend the RNA in 20 μl of 1X DNase I buffer and add 1 unit of DNase I.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Add 180 μl of DEPC water to the sample after incubation.
Extract with 200 μl of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol twice.
Extract once more with 200 μl of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol.
Precipitate RNA by adding 20 μl of 3M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 550 μl of 100% ethanol.
Store the solution at -80°C for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm for 20 minutes at 4°C to collect RNA.
Wash the RNA pellet with 1 ml of 75% ethanol.
Carefully aspirate supernatant from tube.
Dry the RNA pellet.
Resuspend the RNA pellet in 20 μl of DEPC-water.
Incubate tubes at 48°C for 45 minutes to synthesize first-strand cDNA.
Incubate tubes at 95°C for 3 minutes to inactivate AMV reverse transcriptase activity.
Denature samples at 94°C for 30 seconds during PCR amplification cycles.
Anneal samples at 55°C for 30 seconds during PCR amplification cycles.
Extend samples at 72°C for 90 seconds during PCR amplification cycles.
Incubate samples at 72°C for 7 minutes after completing PCR cycles.
Analyze PCR products by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Visualize PCR products using ethidium bromide staining.
Resuspend the RNA pellet in DEPC-water and RS buffer.
Incubate samples at 55°C for 10 minutes, then cool on ice.
Add 2 μl of 10X RNA loading dye to each sample.
Load samples onto a 1% agarose gel containing formaldehyde.
Run the gel at 120 volts for 3 hours with a peristaltic pump recirculating running buffer between electrodes.
Soak the gel in autoclaved water for 15 minutes, changing the water three times.
Denature the gel by immersing it completely in 50 mM NaOH for 20 minutes.
Neutralize the gel in 100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.0-7.6) for 20 minutes.
Soak the gel in 10X SSC for 15 minutes.
Prepare nylon membrane by cutting to the size of the gel.
Soak the membrane in 100 ml of 10X SSC.
Stack at least 3 inches of cut-to-size paper towels in a Pyrex tray.
Soak 3 pieces of Whatman paper in 10X SSC for 3 min, and lay them on top of paper towels.
Place the nylon membrane on top of the Whatman paper.
Lay gel top-side facing upward, and remove bubbles between gel and membrane.
Soak 3 pieces of WhatMan paper in 10X SSC for 3 min, and lay them on top of the gel.
Add 20X SSC to two reservoirs, and place one on each side of the Pyrex tray.
Soak a long piece of Whatman paper in 20X SSC for use as a wick.
Lay the wick on top of the WhatMan paper with ends dipping into the reservoirs.
Place a plastic or glass plate on top of the wick.
Weigh the whole set-up with 4 plastic bottles, each containing 100 ml of water.
Allow the RNA to transfer overnight.
Lift the nylon membrane and rinse briefly in 10X SSC.
Place the nylon membrane on Whatman paper with the RNA side facing upwards.
Cross-link RNA to the nylon membrane using a UV cross-linker at 120 mjoules/cm².
Put the membrane in a heat-sealable bag.
Add pre-hybridization solution to the bag and seal it.
Incubate the bag at 43°C for 1-4 h in a slowly shaking water bath.
Label the DNA fragment with [alpha-³²P]dCTP using the RediPrime II kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Purify the radiolabeled probe from unincorporated nucleotide using the NICK column according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Use 1 μl of probe to determine the counts with a scintillation counter.
Calculate the total incorporation of [alpha-³²P]dCTP and the specific radioactivity of the probe.
Replace the heat-sealable bag with hybridization solution.
Denature the probe by placing it in a boiling water bath for 5 min followed by snap cooling on ice.
Briefly spin down the probe.
Add denatured probe to the bag and seal it.
Continue hybridization overnight at 43°C in a water bath with slow agitation.
Remove the nylon membrane from the bag to a Rubbermaid container.
Rinse the membrane briefly with 6X SSC/0.1%SDS twice.
Wash the membrane three times, each for 15 minutes at room temperature, using 6X SSC/0.1%SDS.
Wash the membrane once at 43°C for 15 minutes using 6X SSC/0.1%SDS.
Wash the membrane with 0.1X SSC/0.1% SDS at room temperature, two or three times, each for 15 minutes.
Check the background of the membrane using a Geiger Counter.
If the background is high, continue washing the membrane with 0.1X SSC/0.1% SDS at 43°C for 15 minutes.
Remove the membrane from the wash solution.
Wrap the membrane with plastic wrap.
Place the wrapped membrane onto a PhosphorImager cassette and flatten it against a PhosphorImager screen.
Depending on hybrid yield and specific activity of the probe, scan the screen for an appropriate amount of time.
Analyze the data with ImageQuant software.
